phase_0.decision: docling-pdf is built from a two-commit fork of docling.rs 2.3.0 so that a phrase that changes font is extracted as one run, as docling-parse 7.21 and later do, and a blank cell is never taken for overpaint on the text-layer path.
phase_0.covers: docling-pdf, docling-core and docling-onnx 2.3.0 are built from the fork https://github.com/Heyoub/docling.rs, branch okf/docling-2.3.0-font-runs, at the commit the [patch.crates-io] section of Cargo.toml names by rev (Cargo.lock records it as their source): two commits on the upstream docling.rs commit that crates.io publishes as 2.3.0. docling-core and docling-onnx come from the same tree so that Cargo.lock holds one of each, and docling is 2.3.0 from crates.io. The first rule changed: in the line contraction of docling-pdf (dp_lines.rs, applicable) a change of font no longer ends a line cell; word cells still end at a change of font. Upstream docling-parse made this change in #351 (7.21.0), and docling.rs has not ported it (upstream master v2.3.0, 2026-10-08). The second: on the text-layer path (textparse.rs, drop_overpainted_cells) a blank cell is never paired as overpaint; with the first change alone, a checkbox glyph, a space and option text in another font merge into one line whose blank cell lies inside it, and the whole line was dropped (measured 2026-10-08: 2,978 to 1,507 non-space characters on upstream table_mislabeled_as_picture.pdf with the first change alone on 1.93.6; every character back with the second; no change on this repository's fixtures). The fork first carried the first change on 1.93.6 (owner decision 2026-10-06); it moved to 2.3.0 on 2026-10-08 after the Docling qualification on 2.3.0 with both changes matched every criterion of the 1.93.6 receipt. A pull request with both changes is drafted on the fork (branch okf/upstream-pr-draft). Nothing was reported upstream. The patch is removed, and the three crates return to crates.io, when a docling.rs release carries both changes.

phase_0.covers: Every CI run starts from a fresh clone of the pushed commit: bootstrap installs from the committed lockfiles only, builds the generator, generates, and builds and type-checks the UI before the gated steps run, so nothing can depend on an uncommitted file. Cargo's registry and target directory are restored from a cache keyed on rust-toolchain.toml and Cargo.lock, with a fallback to the newest cargo cache of the same runner OS when none has that key, so `target` can come from another lockfile state and cargo's own fingerprints under `--locked` decide what is rebuilt; Bun's install cache is keyed on .bun-version and bun.lock and has no fallback. CI asserts that the checkout is unchanged directly after bootstrap (the deterministic-foundation gate) and not again after the gated steps, and it does not run the audit; `bun scripts/dev.mjs clean-checkout` asserts a clean tree after the whole sequence and runs the audit locally, and is a tool, not a gate.

construction.meaning: First work of the next stage, before the storage, ingest and views lanes start: the contract can express every SPEC sentence about extraction, sources and views; the core ports follow in core-ports-carry-extraction-and-views. Missing in the contract today: extraction state on ItemSummary, ItemDocument and SourceAppearance, with a typed failure reason; converter, version, settings and model identity on the wire; page and box locators in Selection, with locator kinds per format; a tabular type for a View's materialized dataset. Owner decisions it carries, 2026-10-05: when a later re-extraction succeeds for a file whose text an agent supplied, the converter's text is shown and indexed by default, the agent's text stays in history and a person may keep it; no chart reads agent-supplied numbers before a person approves them; sending originals to a connected AI is a separate switch, off by default; a damaged PDF is refused clearly and recovery is decided in the ingest lane; unprocessed files (failed, unsupported or partial) are listable by people and by a connected agent, and an agent may propose extracted text as its own proposal kind labelled as supplied by an agent, applied only on approval. 2026-10-06: local mode keeps upload and import and never reorganizes an existing directory in place; a snapshot conflict is resolved per item, keep mine or take theirs, with a diff; status words are OKF's Draft, Stable and Deprecated, with Archived as a separate flag; an app review is written into the file as OKF verified on export, and an imported verified is an unconfirmed claim; the item id is in the file's header; a source card is named from the original name with its extension joined by a hyphen (report.pdf becomes report-pdf.md) and its header carries the original name; an imported file whose header does not parse needs attention and blocks nothing. 2026-10-07: a partly converted file stays readable, names its unconverted pages, is listed as unprocessed, and a retry converts only those pages. 2026-10-08: instants are UTC RFC 3339 `date-time` on the wire; every source location records its provenance (direct, inferred, unresolved); WorkspacePath refuses Windows reserved names, trailing dots and spaces, and NFC and case collisions; EventKind gains security events (connector issued and revoked, sign-in, permission denied); Archive and Purge operations as SPEC §8 states them, workspace purge first

After contract-expresses-extraction-sources-views and before the ingest and views lanes start: the core ports carry what that gate puts on the wire (Stage 1b design section 9). Core carries: the Converter port converting one-based page windows in a child process under a memory cap, with page_count, limits and per-window coverage, and the retained ConversionRecord (line-to-location map, tables, retained assets with role and location, one structured export per window); JobSpec::Import settings, Redigest pages, RestoreWorkspace from an upload, tenant-scoped jobs and artifacts (JobScope), the lease-renewing update_progress heartbeat, purge records, the revision map and derived-object records; source cards that show the contract Extraction (committed pending before conversion by ingest's import handler) and the server-owned application header; the Purger and Backups ports; EventScope and security events; the extraction search filter. Split with application-operations: what dispatch or access can enforce before a handler belongs here and is enforced or provided as core functions with tests: route refusal of DRAFT_BEARING and HUMAN_SESSION_ONLY operations, permission_denied recording, the job-kind rule (access::authorize_job_kind), object ownership (reading::authorize_object), the revision-map check, citation locations, the header refusals (items), the dataset producer (views::materialize and retain_dataset) and schema validation of stored values (stored::decode_stored). Calling them from the operation handlers is application-operations

VersionStore (trailer, find_commit: commit is idempotent on MutationId, candidates), BlobStore, WorkspaceCatalog, SQLite stores (Record/Mutation/Draft/Confirmation/SandboxCapability/Proposal/Upload/Event/Credential), SearchIndex (no drafts), local AccessControl
Commit succeeds, mutation complete is never written, retry finds the revision through find_commit and creates no second commit (commit is idempotent on MutationId)
A superseded attempt can neither complete nor release the mutation; both takeover orders are exercised
A confirmation cannot be consumed twice, or for a different revision, digest, action or target
Two editors on one item get independent drafts; the second Snapshot conflicts after the first

SPEC §2: one process owns a data directory's writable Git, SQLite and object stores. It takes an exclusive lock on a file inside the data directory (std `File::try_lock`, stable since Rust 1.89) before any writable store opens and holds it for the process's life; a second process is refused with a clear error. A data directory on a network filesystem is not supported unless qualified

SPEC §2: SQLite schemas migrate with the already-selected `rusqlite_migration` (user_version; `to_latest`, `pending_migrations`), and application-owned on-disk formats carry a version. Startup refuses data newer than it understands without modifying it; before an upgrade it takes a recoverable backup, applies the migration and verifies the result

SPEC §8, workspace purge first: purging a workspace removes its original bytes, derivatives, index entries, historical content and installation-managed backups, and marks the revisions, citations and Views that referred to them as invalidated; it never claims to erase exports, clones or backups outside the application's control. Archive stays reversible and keeps history. Item purge follows with the same guarantees

Production ingest worker hard memory bound; not DOCLING_RS_MAX_MEMORY_MB on DocumentConverter. Conversion runs in a child process with a hard memory cap, in page windows; the cap and the window size are set from a measurement of whole-document against windowed conversion (owner, 2026-10-07)

construction.meaning: Kill and restart against the real RecordStore with JobHandler(&ClaimedJob); no duplicate effect; after restart leases are expired and pending jobs re-enqueued (`expire_leases`, `pending_jobs`); an attempt that dies without a restart is retried after its lease expires.

An item the converter leaves without a location (a PDF caption: the library drops its box) is located through the page text layer by the rule of qualification/docling/src/locate.rs: docling::pdf_text_layer_pages, the one text-layer item with exactly its text on the page of its parent or of its nearest located earlier sibling, with a box that has area and lies inside the page. An item the rule does not find is recorded as unlocated; it is never given a guessed box, and every location records which source gave it. The rule does not guarantee that the box it finds is the item's own: that file states the two known wrong placements (LOCATE_LIMITS), and the harness records each item's distance to the item whose page was searched without applying a threshold. Whether the product bounds that distance is the owner's decision, open until this gate is built

Text the PDF's fonts cannot map to Unicode is detected by the rule of qualification/docling/src/glyphs.rs (the library prints `/` and the glyph's name for each such glyph), is never indexed as words, and its page is reported as partly extracted. The detector has two known limits: it flags real text of the placeholder's shape that stands after a space (`/B747`, `/v100`, `/tmp123`), and it misses a placeholder glued to a preceding character (`x/g12`). A signal from the library that a glyph had no Unicode is preferred to this detector as soon as the library gives one

ApplicationService implements all 77 operations over OperationContext; CLI against a running server. The handlers call the checks core-ports-carry-extraction-and-views provides: retry_job and cancel_job apply access::authorize_job_kind after loading the job; get_object serves only what reading::authorize_object allows; a request naming a revision is checked with reading::check_revision first, and stored citations (reviews, receipts, comments, View bindings) are remapped to the replacement or invalidated when read; citations are filled and compared with reading::cited_locations and fill_locations, and a saved View is stripped of locations; present_view and resolve_view materialize and record each binding's dataset with views::materialize and retain_dataset; create_item, save_draft, set_type and proposal changes apply the items header refusals; export writes verified for current reviews and import reads an incoming verified as imported coverage

views::validate against catalog.schema.json and vega-lite.schema.json plus referential checks, and a binding outside the View's workspace is rejected (`ViewDocument::bindings_outside`); present and saved-view writes call it first
read_item never returns a draft; get_item returns only the caller's own

The production `CandidateCheck` runs `okf-validator` on a staged candidate directory before commit: storage stages the tree and calls the check it is given, and a candidate the check refuses is never committed. Storage and ingest never decide OKF conformance themselves

SPEC §11: the CLI's `mcp --stdio` command is a relay. It forwards each MCP message to the running local service with a connector credential and holds no store of its own; it starts the service when none is running and otherwise connects to the running one, so the service remains the only writer

A revoked WorkOS role is denied within 60 seconds

Autosave through save_draft, Snapshot with Conflict and rebase flow, confirmation for review and accept

SPEC §2 trial, Electrobun first and Tauri 2 if Electrobun fails it: package the server, start and stop it, show the workspace UI in the system web engine, build a signed installer on Windows and macOS and apply one update. Whether installers and updates ship is decided after the trial

Before any installer or image ships models: every model and native library is listed with its upstream source, version, SHA-256 and licence, and the installer verifies that pinned inventory and never discovers a different set. Today the Docling receipt verifies hashes against a machine-local manifest, which proves consistency, not origin or distribution rights. The models-v1 release was re-published under the same tag: on 2026-10-08 seven model graph files (both layout models and five table models) downloaded from it no longer matched the receipt's hashes at the same sizes, while every weights file did; the owner's local copy still matches the receipt exactly and is kept as the pinned reference. So the inventory must pin bytes the project holds, not a mutable release tag

SPEC §7: 10,000 items per workspace, with indexed search at p95 under 500 ms on a warm local index, measured on a deliberately chaotic corpus (duplicates, ambiguous names, malformed files, mixed PDF, Office and Markdown, deep folders, long histories). The reference machine, corpus and query set are fixed when first measured; only then do the numbers become release criteria
